record.heading: claim
record.author: claude_code
record.body:
[DEFINITION] A statement derived from sources (the verses and, in the claims reading, the science reading) that goes beyond their mere text, held in its own plain wording. A quotation is not a claim. Each claim has its sources and a verdict against the wording of the original essay (stands, restated, widened, corrected or new), and is told in the narrative in full, in part or by pointer.

[BACKGROUND] Held in narrative_claim, narrative_claim_source and narrative_claim_telling. Claims are formulated from the observations in stage 5 of the reading of a collection, which is not yet decided; the existing claims come from an earlier method and are not yet cross-linked to the collections.

record.heading: engagement
record.author: claude_code
record.body:
[DEFINITION] A preparatory step inside the path of a collection, run with Engagement.ps1 before the collection is read. It is not the result of the study.

[BACKGROUND] Behaviour rule 127 (the unit of study is the collection) names it as preparatory. Some surface judgements in surface_term carry the judge rule:engagement.
